utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everyone. By the order of the President, on the 18th of May, 2003, I have been appointed as the judge in the current case. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case for the current hearing?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-97-25-A, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Krnojelac, could you hear everything in your own language, what's happening in the courtroom for this hearing? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear you and I can follow, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, please sit down. [Interpretation] Now I would like the appearances, please, starting by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is Anthony Carmona, appearing with me is Ms. Norul Rashid. We appear on behalf of the Prosecution. And our case manager today is Ms. Lourdes Galicia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Now I am turning to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mihajlo Bakrac, attorney, I'm still representing the accused, Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. As you know, the objective of the Status Conference pursuant to Article 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, this is a Status Conference which is supposed to be held within 25 days of the filing of the appeal, and then within the 120 days of the last Status Conference. In the current case, the appeals filings have been filed by the Defence on the 12th of April, 2002, and by the Prosecutor, at the last Status Conference was held on the 3rd of April, 2003. The objective of the Status Conference is to allow all the people detained, and who are in the course of the appeals procedure, to raise certain issues that are to do with detention, and also issues in relation to their mental and physical condition. So I'm going to now ask Mr. Krnojelac to ask him to speak now directly or through his counsel regarding any issues to do with detention or to do with his physical condition and his health. You have the floor, either Mr. Krnojelac or his Defence representative. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for your words. I hope you won't hold it against me that I won't be able to answer fully your question. As far as my health is concerned, doctors would be able to provide you with a full answer. All I'm going to tell you is that recently, I've had headaches, that I feel increased tension and anxiety, and that I haven't been sleeping too well recently. All this is probably due to my advanced age. As far as the rest is concerned, that is the conditions in the detention unit and the staff there, I don't have any complaints about those. So much from me at this moment, and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may be seated. Now, Mr. Krnojelac, I would like to remind you, pursuant to Articles 84 and 85 of the Rules of the detention, you can of course at any moment submit a request or a complaint, depending on the circumstances, to the head of the Detention Unit, and if necessary, to the Registrar. I would now like to look at the situation of the appeal. Now if we look at the status of the appeal, the Appeals Chamber has heard the oral arguments of the parties at the hearing, at the appeals hearing, that was held on the 14th and 15th of May, 2003. The appeal proceedings having been thus completed, I have no particular questions to address to the parties. However, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any observations to make or any questions they would like to raise with me now. Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any questions. I don't have any issues to raise at this moment, and if you will allow me, I hope I won't be too impertinent because I'm not here to ask questions to be answered by the Chamber, but I would like to communicate the message from my client, I suppose, that his anxiety and tensions are the result of a certain uncertainty. I apologise once again but I would like to ask you whether we can -- and when can we expect the ruling of the Appeals Chamber? I hope I have not overstepped my -- what I'm supposed to do, what I'm required to do, but this is just the consequence of the conversation that I've had with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bakrac, no, not at all. I'm going to reply to you after I have asked the Prosecutor whether he had any questions or issues to raise, and then I will answer the question that you have just asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. CARMONA
utterances.text: Your Honour, respectfully, we have none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GUNEY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Bakrac, regarding the question that you have raised, a priori, the Appeals Chamber would like to have their decision at the beginning of autumn. The parties will certainly be timely informed when the time comes and thus, that will be done through an order, depending on the calendar, and all that will be publicly announced, and that's all. If there are any observations to make or any other questions to ask? No? Very well. Then considering there are no other issues or questions, the current Status Conference can now be adjourned. So we are adjourned. Thank you.
